subject: [PATCH v3 3/7] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode

2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA balancing code to scan read-only file mappings when tiering is enabled, but only for promotion purposes. It keeps the existing restriction on excluding shared libraries from migration. The change allows hot files to be promoted to faster memory tiers, improving performance in certain workloads.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) questioned the necessity of updating placement_scan and suggested an alternative approach by introducing a new variable balancing to simplify the logic and avoid potential issues.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a potential issue with the patch's logic, specifically the handling of shared library pages and read-only file-backed mappings in tiering mode, but did not commit to revising the code immediately.

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) balancing code to scan read-only file mappings when tiering is enabled, but only for promotion purposes. This change prevents hot file folios on slow memory from being promoted and ensures that shared library pages are not migrated unless it would be beneficial. The patch also updates the task_numa_work function to build protection flags for each VMA based on a snapshot of the balancing mode, ensuring consistency in PTE and PMD paths during scanning. This change addresses an issue where a binary's tier residency was not tracking its runtime hotness correctly.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David suggested a minor code reorganization for better readability, specifically moving two conditions related to placement scans into a single variable and then using that variable in the if statement.
